system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller material:** opposing counsel's draft – reviewed against our playbook, not adopted. Nothing in the Seller's package has been accepted, and no fallback authority from Amelia Frost has been given on any item.

**Headline:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" – it departs from our playbook on essentially every negotiated point, and on several points the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the reassurances in the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses). We should return a full mark-up and use those internal inconsistencies as leverage.

---

## A. Liability architecture

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Departure / action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | Seller has landed on our *conditional fallback*. It is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft – none exists. Revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5× ours. Revert. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, **excess-only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** | 5× ours, and deductible rather than tipping. Both changes materially erode recovery – excess-only alone costs us AUD 250k on every successful aggregate claim. Revert both. |
| **Claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval – none given. Revert to 24 months. |
| **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 13)** | Blanket override | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate | This is a hidden general-regime override. It would sweep Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific-indemnity and covenant claims into the 20% / 18-month / basket regime by default. Delete and replace with the reverse default: general limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and are expressly disapplied for every other category. |

**Reasoning:** Every number has moved against us and the structural language (cl 13) is designed so that even if we win back the carve-outs individually, the drafting default re-captures them. The structural point is more important than any single number – fix cl 13 first.

## B. Fundamental / Title claims

**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
**Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
**Action:** Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title to the shares we are paying AUD 24m for at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month fuse. This is a non-negotiable in our playbook.

## C. Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

**Seller:** limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "apply to all Claims of any nature".
**Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
**Action:** There is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller's draft. Insert an express carve-out across cl 9.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5. Under NSW law a clause purporting to exclude liability for a party's own fraud is likely unenforceable anyway, but we should not rely on that – an express carve-out is standard and the Seller cannot credibly resist it. No member of our team has authority to concede this.

## D. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)

**Seller:** general disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (§1.1–1.2).
**Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Action:** Delete §1.1 and §1.2 as general disclosures against the Warranties. Require that a matter is disclosed only if fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Note §1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable in itself, but it cuts both ways – the Seller cannot both disclose a matter to qualify a warranty and deny it is material.

## E. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

**Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
**Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Action:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. Combined with §1.1 general disclosure, this clause would mean anything in the data room is simultaneously "disclosed" *and* "known" – a double bar. "Discoverable" is effectively a prudent-search deemed-knowledge standard, which we reject. If a knowledge concept survives anywhere, it is the *Seller's* awareness (named individuals, after due enquiry) qualifying specified warranties only.

## F. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – material

**Seller Update:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.
**Disclosure Letter §2:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); consent clause 11.2 **with conditions in 11.3**; the Seller has **NOT** included a final written consent **or** evidence the conditions are satisfied.
**Playbook:** effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Action:**
- Make effective Bluefen consent (unconditional, or with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced) a Condition Precedent in Buyer's favour.
- Replace "reasonable endeavours" with "all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours" plus a positive obligation to procure.
- Reject "satisfied on delivery" – a consent delivered subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions is not a consent.
- Point out the contradiction between the Update ("addressed") and the Disclosure Letter (not obtained).

## G. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – material

**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter §3:** not repaid; no discharge of security included; change-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2 in play.
**Playbook:** current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
**Action:**
- Debt-free/cash-free means Riverlark is repaid at Completion out of the price, by direction to the bank, with PPSR/charge releases and discharge under cl 9.2 delivered at Completion.
- Require a payout letter dated within a short window before Completion.
- Reject the post-completion release as drafted. A post-completion mechanic is only available if (i) Riverlark gives an irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of the payout figure and (ii) Amelia Frost approves in writing. Neither exists.
- Check cl 8.1 (change of control) – the bank's consent may itself be needed if there is any gap between Completion and discharge.

## H. Employee bonuses (DD-005) – funds flow

**Seller:** AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
**Disclosure Letter §5:** conditional on Completion and continued employment; not in the funds flow; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Action:** "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually funds it. The bonuses are triggered by Completion and will be a Company liability post-Completion. Require either (a) a specific funds-flow line deducting AUD 420,000 plus payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and any other on-costs from the price, or (b) a Seller covenant to fund them (with on-costs) backed by a specific indemnity outside the general caps. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost figures now.

## I. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate".
**Disclosure Letter §4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 – SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment on file.
**Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
**Action:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover any failure of title to, or claim concerning, the SOW3 Project Materials (including third-party IP claims, costs of securing assignment, and loss of use), not merely the fee.
- Preserve the cure: pre-Completion covenant to pay any outstanding SOW3 fees and procure a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, delivered at Completion.
- Request independent evidence (bank statement / Ironquay confirmation) of whether the AUD 180,000 is paid. Do not price it either way yet.

## J. Export / privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter §6:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; notification question unresolved; investigation preliminary.
**Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
**Action:** Do not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation and do not assert a breach ourselves. Require: (i) pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and link-access data; (ii) completion of a documented investigation (access logs, recipient confirmation of deletion); (iii) ongoing updates and immediate notice of any OAIC/regulator engagement; (iv) a specific indemnity for notification, remediation and regulatory costs *if* the incident is later determined to be notifiable – sitting outside the general cap. No price adjustment at this stage.

## K. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)

**Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure Letter §8:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000); disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Action:** Request renewal dates, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued but unpaid at Completion. If accrued pre-Completion they belong in working capital/Debt-like items; if genuinely forward-looking ordinary-course costs, no adjustment. Reserve position.

## L. Tax / IP warranties

**Seller:** "settled under the general regime".
**Playbook:** terms remain OPEN; separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution.
**Action:** Reject the characterisation – nothing is settled. Tax and IP must have their own regimes (typically longer periods tied to tax limitation periods, separate caps), expressly carved out of cl 13's blanket override. Do not overstate: we are not seeking unlimited liability, but we are not accepting 20%/18 months/basket either.

## M. Title evidence

**Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
**Disclosure Letter §10:** explicitly concedes DD-012 is the source relied on and does not state the Buyer has verified it.
**Playbook:** independent evidence; DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof.
**Action:** Obtain current ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, constitution, share certificates, board minutes approving the sale and Seller authority/capacity evidence, and a certified register at Completion. Title warranties remain Fundamental (section B).

## N. Lower-priority disclosures

- **Office lease (DD-007 §7):** notification-only. Confirm the notice is given pre-Completion and that no consent or change-of-control trigger exists. Minor.
- **Mossvale (DD-009 §9):** assignment restriction, not expressly a share-sale consent. Verify there is no change-of-control clause; obtain a warranty that no counterparty consent is required beyond those listed. Minor.
- **§11 Reservation:** confirms the Seller is not offering any conclusions – consistent with our approach of evaluating the facts ourselves.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the liability package in full** – 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24-month period. No fallback authority exists; do not signal flexibility.
2. **Delete the cl 13 "all Claims" default** and reverse it: general limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims.
3. **Fundamental/Title**: separate regime – 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge. Non-negotiable.
4. **Insert a full fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** across caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
5. **Delete general data-room/public-register disclosure (§1.1–1.2)** – specific fair disclosure only.
6. **Delete cl 8.3** buyer/adviser knowledge bar entirely.
7. **Bluefen**: CP in our favour – effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are rejected.
8. **Riverlark**: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds by direction, security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
9. **Bonuses**: AUD 420k + on-costs as a specific funds-flow deduction or seller-funded with specific indemnity; obtain on-cost figures.
10. **Ironquay**: broaden the indemnity to title/claims over SOW3 materials; covenant to pay outstanding fees and deliver confirmatory assignment; seek independent payment evidence.
11. **DD-006**: log preservation, investigation, update covenants and a contingent specific indemnity; no breach assumed, no price adjustment.
12. **Sandbar**: information request; reserve position; no automatic Debt treatment.
13. **Tax/IP**: expressly open, separate regimes, carved out of the general override.
14. **Title**: independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; DD-012 is not sufficient.
15. **Negotiation point**: the Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller Update on Bluefen, Riverlark and bonuses. Lead the mark-up with those inconsistencies – they undermine the Seller's "fair and balanced" framing and justify our refusal to move on the liability package.

**Escalation:** Nothing in this review requires Amelia Frost's approval because we are reverting to opening positions throughout. If the Seller later presses on the cap or claims period, those are the only two items with a defined fallback, and each needs her written authority identifying the specific draft before it is offered.
=== END ADVICE ===
